title: Neocloud Supply OS
summary: An agent-first operating system concept for a neocloud's supply chain, from GPU sourcing and data center build to logistics and third-party risk, with a static simulation and negotiation demo.

contribution.roleNote: Risk-provider MCP patterns credited to the supplier-risk playbook in isislcn/Hazard-and-Suppliers; simulation and negotiation concepts from CoLab projects.

narrative.problem: A neocloud turning signed customer demand into powered, revenue-earning GPU capacity has to coordinate chips, hardware, data center construction, logistics, asset lifecycle and third-party risk, typically across a portfolio of about 140 separate legacy applications.
narrative.decision: The design names no third-party risk provider: every risk call goes through eleven canonical capabilities behind a RISK_PROVIDER variable, and a registry maps each capability to a provider's native MCP tool or API call.
narrative.tradeoff: Provider function names do not converge (only get_entity matches exactly), so each provider needs a hand-built mapping that records how every native name is known, and the standard is fixed at the capability level rather than the tool level.
narrative.limitation: The concept is signed off but the specification awaits human review with 33 open questions, 11 of them blocking. There is no production code; the economic estimates in the simulation need operational calibration before use in a business case.
narrative.caveat: All data on the site is simulated: suppliers, counterparties and risk-provider signals are fictional and no provider is called. Brand themes are approximations, not affiliated with or endorsed by any company.
